svg.aria-label: CRISPR-Cas9: a guide RNA leads Cas9 to a matching DNA site next to an NGG PAM, Cas9 cuts both strands, and the break is repaired either by error-prone NHEJ that disrupts the gene or by HDR that copies in a donor template
svg.title: CRISPR-Cas9 cut and the two repair outcomes

rect.style: fill:color-mix(in srgb, var(--amber,#f59e0b) 18%, transparent);stroke:color-mix(in srgb, var(--amber,#f59e0b) 60%, transparent);stroke-width:2;stroke-dasharray:6 4
fill:color-mix(in srgb, var(--coral,#ef4444) 22%, transparent);stroke:color-mix(in srgb, var(--coral,#ef4444) 45%, transparent);stroke-width:1.5
fill:color-mix(in srgb, var(--green,#10b981) 22%, transparent);stroke:color-mix(in srgb, var(--green,#10b981) 45%, transparent);stroke-width:1.5

g.text: Ends glued back, often with small insertions
or deletions → frameshift → gene knocked out
Donor with homology arms is copied in →
Cas9 cuts only where the 20-nt spacer matches the DNA and an NGG PAM follows it (SpCas9).
NHEJ is the default, error-prone route; HDR needs a supplied donor template and is less efficient.
